newsitem.title: USA: Prudential gets over 1 million claim form requests.
newsitem.headline: Prudential gets over 1 million claim form requests.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co. of America said Wednesday more than 1 million policyholders have expressed interest in receiving restitution from the company in a class-action settlement stemming from the company's sales practices.

Prudential said it is impossible at this stage to estimate how many policholders will receive remedies in the settlement. However, if based on early average restitution figures of $2,300 per person, Prudential could end up paying more than $2.5 billion if all 1.1 million policyholders submit forms and qualify.
The restitution process was set up as part of the settlement of allegations that Prudential sales agents misled policyholders about what they were purchasing.
The settlement was approved by the U.S. District Court in Newark, N.J., in March.
Under the settlement, people who purchased as many as 10.7 million permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995 were eligible for restitution.
Prudential said it has received 1.1 million requests for the claim forms necessary to file a claim in the alternative dispute resolution (ADR) process.
The ADR process offers policyholders, at no cost, the possibility of least a partial refund plus interest.
Prudential also said it has received 492,349 requests for basic claim relief. Basic claim relief offers policyholders enhanced life insurance, annuities and low-cost premium loans.
Prudential said it has reported these numbers to the state regulators, the plaintiffs' counsel and the federal court.
Standard & Poor's in a statement earlier this month said a key factor will be the number of customers who actually file claims and then successfully move through the remediation process.
Standard & Poor's said at the time it was retaining its claims-paying ability rating on Prudential at double-A-minus.
However, if Prudential's bill considerably surpasses $1 billion, its rating could be lowered, Standard & Poor's said.
Prudential has 75 days from the date it received a request for a claim form to send the form to the policyholder.
The policyholder must return the completed form to Prudential in 90 days.
